name: experience-ablation-m3-arm-switch
title: Experience-ablation M3: gate the full runtime memory pack under an experiment arm + control-arm retrieval blocking
description: Milestone M3 of the experience-layer A/B ablation plan (product code, packages/main). Today the sha256-parity render-gate (resolveHintMode + surfaceExperienceHints) covers only the review-entrypoint experience HINTS at two sites; the richer runtime memory PACK (buildMemoryFreshnessPack/renderMemoryFreshnessPack*) is rendered UNGATED at all 8 RuntimeConsumer lifecycle entrypoints (session_brief, dev_memory_start, host_handoff, story_create, story_advance, done_prepare, done_closure, final_response_check). M3 extends the gate to the full pack under an EXPERIMENT ARM: (1) a pure env-based arm resolver (resolveExperienceArm) returning {experimentId, arm: control|treatment} from PROOFBOUND_EXPERIMENT_ARM/PROOFBOUND_EXPERIMENT_ID, or null when not an experiment task; (2) a shared gate that every pack render site routes through — ALWAYS build the pack, RENDER it on treatment (and on non-experiment normal work, preserving current behavior byte-for-byte), SUPPRESS the render on control, and LOG a runtime_memory_pack_surfaced event on BOTH arms with the lossless would-have-surfaced pack digest (the plan's Shadow C = both-arms-compute-and-log, mirroring the existing experience_hint_surfaced design); (3) mechanical control-arm retrieval blocking in command-policy so a control-arm host cannot pull memory via recall/dev_memory_*/playbook_*/learning_*/memory_playbook_* commands. Normal (non-experiment) sessions are unchanged. Memory stays authority=non_authoritative, gateEvidence=false. No change to the experiment fixtures/protocol/ledger (S1/M1); this is the product-side switch those artifacts drive.
